g1.label: 1. Where does Maria live?
g1.why: The text says Maria lives in Anchorage, Alaska.

g2.label: 2. What is Alaska famous for?
g2.why: The text describes Alaska as famous for its mountains, forests and wild animals.

g3.correct: plastic bottles, bags and old cans
accept: plastic bottles, bags and old cans
g3.label: 3. What do students collect during Clean Alaska?
g3.why: The text says students collect plastic bottles, bags and old cans.

g4.label: 4. First step of a product life cycle
g4.why: The text says the first step in a product life cycle is collecting raw materials.

g5.label: 5. Where did Maria volunteer?
g5.why: The text says Maria volunteered at a wildlife centre last month.

g6.label: 6. Why does Maria enjoy volunteering?
g6.why: The text says Maria enjoys volunteering because she likes helping animals.

g1.label: 1. Plastic bottles ___ in factories (make)
g1.why: ‘Plastic bottles’ is plural, so the passive uses ‘are made’, not ‘is made’.

g2.label: 2. Rubbish ___ by students (collect)
g2.why: ‘Rubbish’ is uncountable/singular, so the passive uses ‘is collected’.

g3.label: 3. Old paper ___ to the recycling centre (take)
g3.why: ‘Old paper’ is uncountable/singular, so the passive uses ‘is taken’.

g4.label: 4. Baby birds ___ three times a day (feed)
g4.why: ‘Baby birds’ is plural, so the passive uses ‘are fed’.

g5.label: 5. The beaches ___ by volunteers (clean)
g5.why: ‘The beaches’ is plural, so the passive uses ‘are cleaned’.

g6.label: 6. New products ___ in shops (sell)
g6.why: ‘New products’ is plural, so the passive uses ‘are sold’.

g7.label: 7. Alaska ___ by millions of tourists (visit)
g7.why: ‘Alaska’ is singular, so the passive uses ‘is visited’.

g8.label: 8. The animal cages ___ every morning (wash)
g8.why: ‘The animal cages’ is plural, so the passive uses ‘are washed’.

g1.label: 1. ___ rubbish is important (collect)
g1.why: A gerund (-ing form) is used when a verb acts as the subject of a sentence.

g2.label: 2. Maria enjoys ___ (work)
g2.why: ‘Enjoy’ is always followed by the gerund (-ing) form, not the infinitive.

g3.label: 3. ___ in cold water is dangerous (swim)
g3.why: A gerund (-ing form) is used when a verb acts as the subject of a sentence.

g4.label: 4. The students finished ___ (clean)
g4.why: ‘Finish’ is always followed by the gerund (-ing) form.

g5.label: 5. Maria keeps ___ (talk)
g5.why: ‘Keep’ is always followed by the gerund (-ing) form.

g6.label: 6. We should avoid ___ plastic bags (use)
g6.why: ‘Avoid’ is always followed by the gerund (-ing) form.

g7.label: 7. ___ about product life cycles helps (learn)
g7.why: A gerund (-ing form) is used when a verb acts as the subject of a sentence.

g8.label: 8. The volunteers suggested ___ (visit)
g8.why: ‘Suggest’ is always followed by the gerund (-ing) form.
